PAPERS.short: Soderblom Laplace-domain in situ network calibration Helsinki Antwerp SensEURCity 2026
PAPERS.title: Laplace domain dynamic calibration in city-wide sensor networks
PAPERS.pm: PM from deployed urban low-cost sensor networks, alongside temperature, RH and pressure
PAPERS.endpoint: In situ calibration coefficients with Monte Carlo uncertainty; shift detection
PAPERS.affil: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, Finland; VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, Finland
PAPERS.n: A Laplace-domain method estimates pairwise dynamic relationships between sensor signals, separates a medium-related spatial effect, and solves an overdetermined calibration against one known network reference, with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Tested on Helsinki (linked to SMEAR III) and Antwerp (SensEURCity). Coefficients were obtained for temperature, RH and pressure in both networks, but PM calibration was feasible only on restricted sensor subsets because PM signals are localized and weakly correlated. Injected shifts could be flagged when geometry and correlations sufficed. No PM R2 or RMSE in the abstract, so the size of the PM failure cannot be graded. Relevance: direct - a metrology-chain calibration transfer fails first on the measurand networks are built for.

PAPERS.short: Yang UK Biobank life-course PM2.5 constituents COPD asthma LRTI lung cancer 2026
PAPERS.title: Life-Course Exposure to PM(2.5) Constituents and Major Respiratory Diseases: Constituent-Specific Associations and Candidate Immune-Metabolic Signatures in a Large Prospective Cohort.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, SO4, NO3, NH4, OC and EC from CMAQ 1930-2010 linked to birth-to-baseline residential histories
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident COPD, asthma, lower respiratory infection and lung cancer; protein and metabolite mediators
PAPERS.affil: Sun Yat-sen University, China; Sun Yat-sen University, China
PAPERS.n: 47,737 UK Biobank participants with birth-to-baseline residential histories, 13-14 years of follow-up. Per IQR of life-course PM2.5: COPD HR 1.138 (1.069-1.211), asthma 1.171 (1.105-1.241), lower respiratory infection 1.046 (1.002-1.091), lung cancer 1.193 (1.064-1.337). SO4 and EC were positive for all four outcomes; mixture associations held for COPD and asthma. The IQR in ug/m3 is not given in the abstract. Limitation: decades of exposure rest on one retrospective CTM with no available monitor validation for most of the period, and the 47,737 with histories are a selected fraction of the Biobank. Relevance: moderate - composition, not mass, is the signal, which a mass-calibrated optical sensor cannot resolve.

PAPERS.short: Shi CFPS compound dry-hot extremes PM2.5 joint incident CVD China 2026
PAPERS.title: Joint effects of air pollution and compound dry-hot extremes on cardiovascular disease risk across adults: a cohort study in China.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 with PM1, PM10, NO2 and O3; exposure source not stated in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident cardiovascular disease and coronary heart disease
PAPERS.affil: First People's Hospital of Xiaoshan District, Wenzhou Medical University, China; First People's Hospital of Xiaoshan District, Wenzhou Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: China Family Panel Studies, 9,265 adults with 69,297 repeated observations, 2010-2018, mixed-effects Cox. Per IQR, PM2.5 HR 1.54 (1.42-1.67) for CVD and 1.75 (1.46-2.11) for coronary disease; dry-hot cumulative days HR 1.30 (1.20-1.41). Concurrent high exposure to both gave a joint HR of 1.92 (1.67-2.21), called synergistic, and repeated across PM1, PM10, NO2 and O3. Limitation: an IQR HR of 1.54 is far above the cohort literature and neither the IQR nor the exposure source is stated; the abstract does not specify how CVD was ascertained; joint exposure and synergy are different quantities, and no interaction scale is given. Relevance: low - no measurement content, but a compound-exposure design that a network could sharpen.

PAPERS.short: Myers NIOSH CWHSP pneumoconiosis dusty job type underground coal 1991-2024
PAPERS.title: Assessment of pneumoconiosis by dusty job type among underground coal miners participating in the Coal Workers' Health Surveillance Program,1991-2024.
PAPERS.pm: Respirable coal mine dust, proxied by occupation and region; no dust measurement in the analysis
PAPERS.endpoint: Radiographic coal workers' pneumoconiosis and progressive massive fibrosis
PAPERS.affil: NIOSH Respiratory Health Division, USA; NIOSH Respiratory Health Division, USA
PAPERS.n: 30,319 underground miners in the national surveillance programme, 1991-2024, tenure-adjusted. Continuous miner operators had CWP PR 1.8 (1.6-2.0) and PMF PR 3.0 (2.3-4.0) against those never in the job; roof bolters 1.4 (1.3-1.6) and 1.4 (1.1-1.9). CWP prevalence was 8.4% in Central Appalachia versus 1.5% elsewhere, adjusted PR 3.9 (3.4-4.5); PMF PR 10 (5.7-17.5). Limitation: job title stands in for dust, and programme participants are self-selected, so healthy-worker and participation bias run in unknown directions. Prevalence pools 33 years of changing limits. Relevance: moderate - a tenfold regional contrast in a monitored regulated industry is the strongest argument today for personal rather than compliance-point dust data.

PAPERS.short: Molina Rueda AirPen facility-wide personal PM noise formaldehyde one shift 2026
PAPERS.title: Facility-wide assessment of occupational exposure to dust, noise, and formaldehyde
PAPERS.pm: Total particulate by personal AirPen sampler with on-board sensors, plus formaldehyde and A-weighted noise
PAPERS.endpoint: Exposure distribution parameters (mean, geometric mean, 95th percentile) and their uncertainty
PAPERS.affil: Colorado State University, USA; Colorado State University, USA
PAPERS.n: Five people deployed 83 AirPen compact personal monitors across one full shift at a furniture plant of about 100 workers. Valid after screening: 67 PM, 67 noise, 22 formaldehyde (72, 67, 31 counting samples below the LOD). On-board sensors identified anomalies and confirmed wear. Distribution parameters were estimated with high certainty, and confidence intervals grew several-fold when fewer samples were analysed. Limitation: one facility on one shift says nothing about day-to-day variance, usually the main occupational term; 16 of 83 PM samples were lost or below LOD, and no comparison values are in the abstract. Relevance: direct - sample count, not instrument class, sets the uncertainty. \textsc{backfill}, entry 28 May 2026.

PAPERS.short: Kloppenborg ARMIE SPS30 node laboratory DustTrak SMPS APS source-out calibration 2026
PAPERS.title: Laboratory Evaluation of ARMIE, a Portable SPS30-Based Low-Cost Sensor Node for PM2.5 Monitoring
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 from Sensirion SPS30 in a portable node, against DustTrak and combined SMPS+APS
PAPERS.endpoint: Agreement, calibration error and limits of agreement by leave-one-sensor-out and leave-one-source-out
PAPERS.affil: Aarhus University, Denmark; Aarhus University, Denmark
PAPERS.n: SPS30 nodes were co-located in the laboratory with a DustTrak and an SMPS+APS across candle, cooking, cigarette smoke and clean air, at regular and high humidity. Agreement with the DustTrak was r 0.93-0.98; with SMPS+APS it was moderate, r 0.74-0.94, with systematic underestimation at high concentration. Leave-one-sensor-out and leave-one-source-out calibration reduced mean error and narrowed limits of agreement. Limitation: a DustTrak is itself a photometer, so the high r partly reflects shared optical bias; the sizing reference is the honest comparator and shows the gap. No gravimetric or field arm, and r is not accuracy. Relevance: direct - leave-one-source-out is the right test for epidemiology nodes. \textsc{backfill}, Crossref 2 January 2026.

PAPERS.short: Goyal PurpleAir PA-II kappa-Kohler Lorentz-Lorenz random forest moisture artefact 2026
PAPERS.title: A physics-aware digital twin for correcting moisture-induced material artifacts in PM2.5 sensors
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 from a pair of PurpleAir PA-II units co-located with an EPA FEM monitor (site 220330009)
PAPERS.endpoint: Normalized mean bias and R2 after humidity correction
PAPERS.n: A pair of PA-II units beside one EPA FEM monitor for 150 days in an industrial area. kappa-Kohler growth and a Lorentz-Lorenz refractive index mixing rule motivate features for a polynomial-enhanced random forest. At RH 76.16% optical intensity rose 59.5%, summarised as a mass-intensity divergence factor of 4.33. Raw bias of +17.55% fell to 0.13% NMB, R2 0.9010. Limitation: two sensors at one site, single author, and the abstract gives no train/test separation by time, sensor or site, so 0.13% cannot be read as field skill. Calling FEM 'gravimetric' is loose. Relevance: moderate - the physics is standard and testable; the transferability is untested. \textsc{backfill}, Crossref 26 September 2026.

PAPERS.short: Mao wavelet attention LSTM indoor aerosol concentration prediction 2026
PAPERS.title: A Wavelet-Based Attention LSTM Framework for Aerosol Concentration Prediction in Indoor Environments
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref at issue time, so no finding is asserted. The title describes a wavelet decomposition feeding an attention LSTM to predict indoor aerosol concentration. Carried because short-horizon indoor prediction is one of the candidate edge-inference tasks for a sensor node, and J Aerosol Sci is one of the venues where such work is tied to a measured aerosol. What decides its value is unknown until the abstract deposits: the measuring instrument, whether validation is by held-out episode rather than random split, and the prediction horizon. Relevance: possible, unassessed.

PAPERS.short: Zhu meta-analysis air pollutants allergic rhinitis children PM2.5 TRAP mold 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between exposure to gaseous air pollutants and the risk of allergic rhinitis in children and adolescents: A meta-analysis.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, traffic-related pollution, NO2, O3, SO2, CO and mold as reported by included studies
PAPERS.endpoint: Allergic rhinitis in children and adolescents
PAPERS.affil: Weinan Maternal and Child Health Hospital, China; Beijing Children's Hospital, Capital Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: Meta-analysis of 21 studies (13 cross-sectional, 6 cohort, 2 case-control). Pooled ORs: mold 1.45 (1.16-1.80), traffic-related pollution 1.39 (1.21-1.59), PM2.5 1.23 (1.05-1.43), O3 1.15 (1.05-1.26), NO2 1.09 (1.00-1.17); PM10, SO2 and CO not significant. Estimates for PM10, NO2 and O3 were higher in Chinese studies. Limitation: the abstract gives no exposure increment, so the pooled ratios cannot be compared across pollutants or to any concentration, and 13 of 21 studies are cross-sectional. Mold is not an ambient pollutant, and a 'gaseous' title over a PM2.5 estimate shows loose scoping. Relevance: low - a pooled OR with no increment cannot feed a sensor-based exposure-response.

PAPERS.short: Drummond mini-review climate exposures paediatric lung-function trajectories 2026
PAPERS.title: Climate change as a modifier of paediatric lung-function trajectories.
PAPERS.pm: Air pollution and wildfire smoke among climate-sensitive exposures; no PM metric specified
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung-function trajectory, attained peak and exacerbation-related step-down
PAPERS.affil: University Hospital Necker-Enfants Malades, France; Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland, Ireland
PAPERS.n: Mini-review using lung-function trajectories as its frame. Climate-sensitive exposures shift trajectories downward by three routes: early developmental disruption (gestational pollution and temperature, via growth restriction and preterm birth), sustained exposure impairing postnatal growth and peak, and exacerbations with incomplete recovery. Evidence that cleaner air accelerates lung-function growth is taken as proof the trajectory can be protected. No effect sizes or search method in the abstract. Limitation: co-occurring heat, smoke, allergen and damp are not separated, so attribution to PM is not possible from this frame. Relevance: low - frames why childhood exposure windows matter, without a measurement requirement.

PAPERS.short: Cardenas-Iniguez ABCD linked external data environment review first decade 2026
PAPERS.title: Environmental influences using linked external data in ABCD: A review of the first decade.
PAPERS.pm: Geocoded residential air pollution among linked neighbourhood and policy variables; metric not specified
PAPERS.affil: University of Southern California, USA; University of Southern California, USA
PAPERS.n: Ten years of Linked External Data work in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (~11,800 US youth), covering neighbourhood conditions, built environment, air pollution, greenspace and state policy. The authors conclude that development reflects cumulative influences and that timing and study design bound what can be concluded, and they call for refined geocoding and exposure methods. No effect sizes in the abstract. Limitation: an internal working-group review of its own dataset, and residential geocoding ignores school and transit time, which matters at this age. Relevance: moderate - the largest US neurodevelopment cohort names exposure resolution as a limiting method.

PAPERS.short: Li poultry-house PM2.5-derived material APEC sequential exposure chick cell 2026
PAPERS.title: Inflammatory and redox responses associated with sequential exposure to poultry-house PM2.5-derived material and avian pathogenic Escherichia coli in chicken models.
PAPERS.pm: Autoclaved eluate of broiler-house PM2.5-fraction material, uncharacterized after sterilization
PAPERS.endpoint: Inflammatory, redox, CFTR and autophagy markers in lung cells and chicks
PAPERS.affil: Ludong University, China; Ludong University, China
PAPERS.n: Chicken type II-like lung cells and 40 SPF chicks (n=10/group, 14 days) received control, single or sequential PM2.5-derived material then avian pathogenic E. coli. The sequential group showed the largest changes in several inflammatory and redox endpoints and lower CFTR; N-acetyl-L-cysteine and CBIQ shifted cell responses toward control. No effect sizes in the abstract. Limitation, stated by the authors: the eluted, lyophilized, autoclaved material was not characterized for size, composition or endotoxin, and schedules differed in timing, so no interaction, synergy or particle-specific effect is established. Relevance: low - a sterilized eluate is not an airborne particle.

PAPERS.short: Qureshi narrative review bioaccessibility particle-bound metals PAHs tiered framework 2026
PAPERS.title: Bioaccessibility and Toxicity of Particle-Bound Metals and Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons: Sources, Respiratory Fate, Mechanisms, and Risk Assessment
PAPERS.pm: Particle-bound metals and PAHs; PM mass, size, speciation and oxidative potential
PAPERS.endpoint: Bioaccessibility, oxidative stress and delivered-dose toxicity
PAPERS.affil: International Islamic University Islamabad, Pakistan; International Islamic University Islamabad, Pakistan
PAPERS.n: Single-author critical narrative review, not peer-reviewed. Metal release varies with element, source, size, extraction conditions and solid-to-liquid ratio, and acidic lysosomal fluid usually dissolves more than near-neutral extracellular fluid; PAH release depends on hydrophobicity, soot binding, surfactants and proteins. Poorly soluble particles can stay active with little released. Proposes a tiered framework joining mass, source, size, speciation, compartment-specific bioaccessibility, oxidative potential and delivered dose. No search method or quantitative synthesis in the abstract, and differences in simulated lung fluids limit comparison. Relevance: low - explains why equal mass need not mean equal hazard, beyond what a mass sensor reports.

PAPERS.short: Olsen LC-APCI-MS resin acids personal softwood sawmill dust Norway 2026
PAPERS.title: A Versatile Method for Determination of Resin Acids in Occupational Softwood Sawmill Dust Samples by Liquid Chromatography-Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionization-Mass Spectrometry.
PAPERS.pm: Resin acids in personal wood dust samples
PAPERS.endpoint: Chromatographic separation and quantification of five resin acids and one oxidation product
PAPERS.affil: National Institute of Occupational Health (STAMI), Norway; National Institute of Occupational Health (STAMI), Norway
PAPERS.n: Six reversed-phase columns and multiple mobile phases were screened; a C18-amide column with acetonitrile and 30 mM ammonium acetate at pH 6.30 and negative APCI gave a 15-minute isocratic run. Applied to six personal sawmill dust extracts, it determined abietic, dehydroabietic and levopimaric acids, coeluting isopimaric and pimaric acids, and 7-oxodehydroabietic acid. Limitation: six extracts demonstrate applicability, not exposure levels, and two isomers still coelute despite that being the problem the method targets. LODs are not in the abstract. Relevance: low - constituent chemistry of an occupational dust that no optical sensor could separate, useful only as a reference analysis.

PAPERS.short: Apak office-to-education studio zone CO2 PM2.5 PM10 TVOC perception Istanbul 2026
PAPERS.title: Indoor Air Quality and Occupant Perception in an Office Building Adapted for Educational Use: A Zone‐Based Case Study
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM2.5 and PM10 by sequential point measurement; instrument not named in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Zonal CO2, PM and TVOC; occupant perception by questionnaire
PAPERS.affil: Istanbul Gelisim University, Turkiye; Beykoz University, Turkiye
PAPERS.n: One mechanically ventilated design studio, three zones, questionnaire from 48 users. CO2 was highest and most variable in the central zone (527 +/- 114 ppm, 95th percentile 760 ppm), and upper-end particulate indicators were greater in the circulation zone, but no zonal difference in CO2, PM or TVOC survived multiplicity adjustment. Perceived freshness tracked overall satisfaction (Spearman rho 0.475, 0.219-0.682). Limitation, stated by the authors: respondents cannot be linked to measurement times or locations, so this is no exposure-perception relationship; sequential monitoring and few points restrict inference. Relevance: low - sequential single-instrument sampling cannot resolve within-room PM differences, which simultaneous nodes could.

PAPERS.short: Wu penguin colony chlorophyll-a mediation PM1 PM2.5 PM10 Ardley Island 2026
PAPERS.title: Phytoplankton-mediated coupling between penguin colonies and atmospheric particulate matter in Antarctic coastal waters.
PAPERS.pm: Along-track PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 with seawater chlorophyll-a and nutrients; instrument not named in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Spatial and mediation association of Chl-a with PM
PAPERS.affil: University of Science and Technology of China, China; University of Science and Technology of China, China
PAPERS.n: Synchronous ocean-atmosphere transects around Ardley Island. After controlling for spatial autocorrelation, chlorophyll-a remained associated with PM2.5 (standardized coefficient 0.12). Across PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 indirect NH4-Chl-a-PM effects exceeded direct ones, up to eightfold, but only at alpha 0.10, with 95% CIs including zero. The authors nonetheless propose Chl-a as a proxy for the colony atmospheric footprint. Limitation: the mediation result does not exclude zero, the transects are one spatial sample, and particle composition is not reported, so marine biogenic origin is inferred. Relevance: low - a very clean background where optical PM readings are near any low-cost sensor's noise floor.

PAPERS.short: Kim CMAQ-UNIPAR secondary organic aerosol South Korea ASIA-AQ 2026
PAPERS.title: Prediction of Secondary Organic Aerosol Formation in South Korea using CMAQ-UNIPAR during the ASIA-AQ Campaign
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref at issue time, so no finding is asserted. The title places a CMAQ run with the UNIPAR SOA module against the ASIA-AQ campaign over South Korea. Carried because a mechanistic SOA module tested against an airborne and ground campaign bears on the organic fraction of PM2.5, the component that most changes refractive index and hygroscopicity across a sensor's calibration range, and on the CTM surfaces health cohorts inherit. To be assessed when the Elsevier abstract deposits: bias against campaign OA and any change in simulated PM2.5. Relevance: possible, unassessed.

PAPERS.short: Gantina remote sensing CO HC NOx soot heavy-duty trucks buses Indonesia 2026
PAPERS.title: Emission of CO, HC, NOx, and Soot from HDV Trucks and Buses using Remote Sensing in Indonesia
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Soot from on-road heavy-duty vehicles by remote sensing
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref at issue time, so no finding is asserted. The title reports on-road remote sensing of CO, HC, NOx and soot from heavy-duty trucks and buses in Indonesia. Carried because measured real-world fleet soot factors are scarce for Southeast Asia, and because they anchor inventory inputs where reference networks are thin and low-cost networks are the main expansion route. To be assessed when an abstract deposits: fleet size sampled, soot retrieval method and any emission-standard contrast. Relevance: possible, unassessed.
